name: RoboBench
description: A comprehensive evaluation benchmark for multimodal large language models as embodied brains for robotic manipulation, covering 5 dimensions, 14 capabilities, 25 tasks, and 6092 QA pairs.
creator: Yulin Luo; Chun-Kai Fan; Menghang Dong; Jiayu Shi; Mengdi Zhao; Bo-Wen Zhang; Cheng Chi; Jiaming Liu; Gaole Dai; Rongyu Zhang; Ruichuan An; Kun Wu; Zhengping Che; Shaoxuan Xie; Guocai Yao; Zhongxia Zhao; Pengwei Wang; Guang Liu; Zhongyuan Wang; Tiejun Huang; Shanghang Zhang
citeAs: Luo, Yulin et al. ROBOBENCH: A COMPREHENSIVE EVALUATION BENCHMARK FOR MULTIMODAL LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS AS EMBODIED BRAIN. arXiv:2510.17801v1, 2025.
rai:dataCollection: The benchmark is built from open-source and in-house robotic data to evaluate five cognitive dimensions: instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis. Instruction comprehension uses paired explicit and implicit instructions, where explicit instructions are drawn from daily-life scenarios and implicit instructions are rewritten from them using LLMs. Perception reasoning uses real robot data with type and view metadata, curated static attributes, GPT-generated functional properties and distractors, Gemini-segmented video steps, manual annotations of relative positions and keypoint changes, and human-labeled bounding boxes. Generalized planning is built from high-quality robotic videos, from which frame sequences are extracted as standardized inputs. Affordance prediction samples representative frames from the planning pool and annotates static, dynamic, and mobile affordances. Failure analysis uses execution-level failures collected from RoboMIND and planning-level failures synthesized by perturbing correct instructions.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Document analysis, Others
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Open-source and in-house robotic data; large-scale real-world robotic datasets; high-quality robotic videos; real robot data with type and view metadata; execution-level failures from RoboMIND; curated static attributes from Gao et al. (2024). The paper also states that planning data draw from large-scale real robotic data and in-house collection, and planning tasks use sources such as Open X-Embodiment, RH20T, RoboMIND, and other cited robotic datasets.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Planning-level failures are synthesized by perturbing correct instructions, including wrong object, missing step, and wrong order. For planning, each step is mapped into function templates such as pick_up(object) and move_to(object, target), grouped into manipulation or navigation skill lists. Frame sequences are extracted as standardized inputs. All perception data are standardized into multiple-choice QA.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The construction pipeline generally follows preprocessing, annotation with VLMs, detection models or human experts, and QA format generation. General and task-specific filters are applied during construction: general criteria address image quality and task validity, and sub-benchmarks have tailored rules such as excluding single-arm data from dual-arm tasks. For planning, frame sequences are extracted from videos as standardized inputs. After construction, 20 professionally trained annotators inspect items for linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness. A majority-vote strategy is used: items that all models solve correctly are removed, and items all models fail to solve undergo manual review and correction.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations are produced by both models and humans. For planning, Gemini generates structured annotations including task summaries, step-wise instructions with timestamps, and metadata such as objects, actions, scenes, and embodiments; these are refined by human annotators. Perception reasoning uses GPT-generated functional properties and distractors, Gemini-segmented video steps, manual annotations of relative positions and keypoint changes, and human-labeled bounding boxes linking instructions to target objects. Affordance prediction annotates representative frames with static contact points, dynamic motion trajectories, and mobile base positions. Failure analysis uses expert labels for execution-level failures. Human annotators also conduct post-construction quality inspections.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A two-stage quality control process is used: filtering during construction and post-construction validation. After data construction, 20 professionally trained annotators validate linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness. A majority-vote strategy is adopted: items that all models solve correctly are removed, while items all models fail to solve are manually reviewed and corrected. For metric validation, a human study uniformly sampled 438 long-horizon tasks from Q1 planning inference sets, and expert annotators assigned holistic scores from 0 to 20; the proposed automated metric showed higher Pearson correlation with human judgments than an LLM-based pairwise trajectory scoring baseline.
rai:annotatorDemographics: 20 professionally trained annotators; expert annotators with prior training
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini, GPT, LLMs, MLLMs, VLMs, detection models
rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to quantify high-level cognition, clarify the role of the embodied brain, and guide the development of next-generation MLLMs toward more robust robotic intelligence. The paper positions RoboBench as a unified scaffold for measuring embodied cognition and guiding development of more robust, generalizable embodied intelligence.
rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that planning-level failures are synthesized by perturbing correct instructions because of a lack of real-world planning failure data. It also states that existing planning data primarily focus on concrete action execution without explicitly distinguishing left-right arm assignments or positional movements, which the authors attribute as a reason current models fail in dual-arm coordination and mobile manipulation. The benchmark also removes items that all models solve correctly and manually reviews items all models fail.
rai:dataLimitations: The paper reports several limitations revealed by the benchmark and task design: current MLLMs show severe degradation on implicit instructions, weak robot-view recognition and temporal grounding, poor dual-arm coordination and rare-object reasoning, shallow affordance prediction, and especially difficult execution-level failure diagnosis. It also notes that execution-level failures require fine-grained distinctions and even human performance is relatively low. Additionally, real-world planning failure data are lacking, so planning-level failures are synthesized.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is a benchmark for evaluating multimodal large language models as embodied brains in robotic manipulation. It is used for systematic evaluation across instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis, and for establishing a leaderboard over state-of-the-art MLLMs. The paper also uses human and text-only LLMs as references.
